text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm drafting alert rules for the new runtime dashboards (latency, kv cache, and model-fallback rates). Need agreement on thresholds + who owns paging routing. :wave:
ben: Thanks — can you post the raw metrics names? I'll map them to current alerting infra. :eyes:
maria: sure — top ones: `runtime.latency_p50`, `runtime.latency_p95`, `kv_cache.hit_rate`, `slo.burn_rate` (per-route), `fallback.rate` (model variant fallback count).
caroline: For SLO burn: propose alert when burn_rate >= 1.5 for 10m -> page, and > 2.5 for 5m -> escalate. Keep 1.2 for dashboard warnings only. Thoughts?
dmitri: +1 to 1.5/10m page. But for routes that are low-traffic we should use relative windows (burn per 1k requests) — otherwise noisy.
frank: We should separate infra-caused latency vs model-caused. Suggest adding tag `cause:runtime|model` upstream in telemetry so alerts can route differently.
ben: Good call. For pager routing: runtime issues -> eng-runtime oncall, model fallback spikes -> eng-ml oncall, kv cache degradations -> eng-infra. Can we encode that in the alert labels?
maria: yes, add label `owner:eng-runtime|eng-ml|eng-infra` depending on `cause`. We'll add a rule that synthesizes owner based on `cause`.
infra-bot: Reminder: new alerts must include runbook link and severity label or they will fail validation. See `#eng-oncall` runbook template. :memo:
caroline: draft alert example (will iterate):
```
alert: SLOBurnHigh
expr: increase(slo.burn_rate{route=~"/api/.*"}[10m]) > 1.5
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
  owner: '{{ cause | default("eng-runtime") }}'
annotations:
  summary: "SLO burn >1.5 for {{ $labels.route }}"
  runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/slo-burn"
```
maria: Nice. Two routing knobs we need to finalize: 1) fallback owner override for model-team when `fallback.rate` > X, 2) per-route mute windows for experimental routes (no page for first 30m after deploy).
frank: For (2) we can reuse existing deploy metadata: `deployment.phase=canary` -> suppress page for 30m but still log. That should limit noise.
dmitri: Also suggest a soft-alert channel (`#ops-notify`) for kv cache hit_rate drops between 0.7 and 0.85 for 15m so infra can triage before paging. Page only if <0.7.
ben: I'll convert these into Prometheus rules and a PagerDuty policy mapping. One ask: which oncall schedule to use for eng-ml? @oncall-rotation-bot can you confirm schedule name?
oncall-rotation-bot: eng-ml uses schedule `ml-primary-us`. eng-runtime uses `runtime-rotating-us`. eng-infra uses `infra-core`.
maria: Perfect. I'll push the PR with rules + dashboard panels. Please review owner label logic in the PR — we will gate merge until oncall agrees. :thumbsup:
caroline: I'm going to add test queries to the dashboard so we can simulate burn spikes before enabling pages. :test_tube:
ben: ETA to PR this afternoon. Will ping for review.
maria: Thanks team — aim to roll to staging tomorrow and enable soft alerts. If no objections by EOD we'll promote to prod on Friday. :rocket:
